analogs.covers: Body and grit: the climbing rat of palm islands, harbours and dry coasts that eats whatever it finds, takes much of its water from its food and gets by where little else does
Voice and temper: a brilliant mimic of dry, open country with a long memory for faces that swoops screeching at anything near its nest and lives in noisy, bickering groups

headline: A black rat with a magpie's voice: the hardy Microraptor of dry rock and salt coasts that gets by on little food and no fresh water, copies every call and dive-bombs anything near its nest.

setting.label: Dry rock and salt coasts without fresh water
setting.note: Hanqiugi hatch in Dry Fang Canyon, Tallbrush Coasts, Crag Bluffs, Coastland Swamp, Mudflats, Coastal Bluffs and Palm Islands. None of them has fresh water: there is only dry rock or salt and brackish water. Border land: Wind Tunnels, East Passage and Steep Run, all equally without fresh water. Everything else is roaming ground. Nests on cliff ledges, bluffs and palms, never in caves.

playsLike: You are a Hanqiugi, the hardy subspecies: you hatched on dry rock or on the salt coast and can go for longer without food and water. You are the smallest carnivore on the roster (Tiny, 500 combat weight, 400 HP, a 40 bite that only hurts targets under 600 combat weight, land sprint 825 for 400 s). You climb trunks and cliffs, glide from tree to tree and sleep in short bursts high up, never in caves. You live on carrion, insects and critters and hunt only Juvenile-and-younger Deinonychus, Latenivenatrix, Psittacosaurus and Struthiomimus, even guarded ones, plus Rhamphorhynchus, with at most one partner. Your weapon is mimicry: copied calls lure the parents away from their nest. In a scurry of up to 10 you swarm and dive-bomb anything that hunts you, except Apex carnivores and the six species you always flee from; as a pair or alone you may claim an Apex carnivore as your companion, ride on its side and learn its calls.

why.text: Hanqiugi “are able to go for longer without food and water”. Black rats live on ships, in harbours and on remote islands on whatever they find (official inspiration: rats).

None of the seven Hanqiugi hatching areas has fresh water: Dry Fang Canyon and Crag Bluffs are dry rock, the rest lie on salt or brackish water. Black rats live on dry islands and atolls and take most of their water from what they eat.
Microraptor nest “in high up locations, such as cliffsides, ledges and treetops”. The black rat is the climbing rat, nesting high in palms and roofs, unlike the burrowing brown rat.
Microraptor “are primarily scavengers and insectivores, but may occasionally attempt to hunt”, just as rats are the classic scavengers of coasts and harbours.

Microraptor “are most commonly known for their mimicry of other species” and parrot calls back at tolerant species in “conversations”. Australian magpies are among the best vocal mimics, copying other birds, dogs and even sirens.

Any intruder on a claimed nest tree is “met immediately with loud, screeching protests, with members swooping overhead repeatedly”: the magpie's swooping season, with small pecks included (official inspiration: magpies).

notLike: Black rats run and climb but cannot glide; Microraptor glides between cliffs, ledges and palms.
Rats breed fast in big litters; a Microraptor clutch holds 2 eggs, a main egg and a spare.
Microraptor has a “general disdain for water”: the salt coast is a place to scavenge and nest above, never to swim in.
twist: The subspecies of hard places: where there is no fresh water and little food, a Hanqiugi still gets by.
